entities.summary: Telesilla was an ancient Greek lyric poet from Argos, active in the fifth century BC. She is known for her supposed role in the defence of Argos in 494 BC, which is doubted by modern scholars. Only a few fragments of her poetry survive, several of which reference the gods Apollo and Artemis. The longest surviving fragment, only two lines, is quoted by the grammarian Hephaestion to illustrate the Telesillan metre, named after her. She was apparently famous in antiquity, included by Antipater of Sidon in his work on Greek poetry. Her legacy extends to the realm of classical poetry, with scholars continuing to study and interpret her works. The Telesillan metre, a unique poetic form, remains a subject of interest among scholars of classical literature. The fragments of her poetry provide a glimpse into the cultural and religious practices of ancient Greece. The mythology surrounding Telesilla's life and poetry continues to captivate scholars and enthusiasts alike. Her significance lies in her contribution to the evolution of classical poetry, making her an important figure in the cultural landscape of ancient Greece.
